source_text: Ὅτι δὲ Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν: Οὐ φάγεσθε χοῖρον οὔτε ἀετὸν οὔτε ὀξύπτερον οὔτε κόρακα οὔτε πάντα ἰχθύν, ὃς οὐκ ἔχει λεπίδα ἐν ἑαυτῷ, τρία ἔλαβεν ἐν τῇ συνέσει δόγματα. πέρας γέ τοι λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν τῷ Δευτερονομίῳ: Καὶ διαθήσομαι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον τὰ δικαιώματά μου. ἄρα οὖν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐντολὴ θεοῦ τὸ μὴ τρώγειν, Μωϋσῆς δὲ ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν. τὸ οὖν χοιρίον πρὸς τοῦτο εἶπεν: οὐ κολληθήσῃ φησίν, ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινές εἰσιν ὅμοιοι χοίρων: τουτέστιν ὅταν σπαταλῶσιν, ἐπιλανθάνονται τοῦ κυρίου, ὅταν δὲ ὑστεροῦνται, ἐπιγινώσκουσιν τὸν κύριον, ὡς καὶ ὁ χοῖρος ὅταν τρώγει τὸν κύριον οὐκ οἶδεν, ὅταν δὲ πεινᾷ κραυγάζει, καὶ λαβὼν πάλιν σιωπᾷ. Οὐδὲ φάγῃ τὸν ἀετὸν οὐδὲ τὸν ὀξύπτερον οὐδὲ τὸν ἰκτῖνα οὐδὲ τὸν κόρακα: οὐ μή, φησίν, κολληθήσῃ οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες οὐκ οἴδασιν διὰ κόπου καὶ ἱδρῶτος πορίζειν ἑαυτοῖς τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἁρπάζουσιν τὰ ἀλλότρια ἐν ἀνομίᾳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπιτηροῦσιν ὡς ἐν ἀκεραιοσύνῃ περιπατοῦντες καὶ περιβλέπονται, τίνα ἐκδύσωσιν διὰ τὴν πλεονεξίαν, ὡς καὶ τὰ ὄρνεα ταῦτα μόνα ἑαυτοῖς οὐ προίζει τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἀργὰ καθήμενα ἐκζητεῖ, πῶς ἀλλοτρίας σάρκας καταφάγῃ, ὄντα λοιμὰ τῇ πονηρίᾳ αὐτῶν. Καὶ οὐ φάγῃ, φησίν, σμύραιναν οὐδὲ πολύποδα οὐδὲ σηπίαν: οὐ μή, φησίν, ὁμοιωθήσῃ κολλώμενος ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες εἰς τέλος εἰσὶν ἀσεβεῖς καὶ κεκριμένοι ἤδη τῷ θανάτῳ, ὡς καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ἰχθύδια μόνα ἐπικατάρατα ἐν τῷ βυθῷ νήχεται, μὴ κολυμβῶντα ὡς τὰ λοιπά, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω τοῦ βυθοῦ κατοικεῖ. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν δασύποδα οὐ φάγῃ. πρὸς τί; οὐ μὴ γένῃ, φησίν, παιδοφθόρος οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις, ὅτι ὁ λαγωὸς κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν πλεονεκτεῖ τὴν ἀφόδευσιν: ὅσα γὰρ ἔτη ζῇ, τοσαύτας ἔχει τρύπας. ἀλλὰ οὐδὲ τὴν ὕαιναν φάγῃ: οὐ μή, φησίν, γένῃ μοιχὸς οὐδὲ φθορεὺς οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις. πρὸς τί; ὅτι τὸ ζῷον τοῦτο παρ ἐνιαυτὸν ἀλλάσσει τὴν φύσιν καὶ ποτὲ μὲν ἄρρεν, ποτὲ δὲ θῆλυ γίνεται. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν γαλῆν ἐμίσησεν καλῶς. οὐ μή, φησίν, γενηθῇς τοιοῦτος, οἵους ἀκούομεν ἀνομίαν ποιοῦντας ἐν τῷ στόματι δἰ ἀκαθαρσίαν, οὐδὲ κολληθήσῃ ταῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ταῖς τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιούσαις ἐν τῷ στόματι. τὸ γὰρ ζῷον τοῦτο τῷ στόματι κύει. περὶ μὲν τῶν βρωμάτων λαβὼν Μωϋσῆς τρία δόγματα οὕτως ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν: οἱ δὲ κατ’ ἐπιθυμίαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὡς περὶ βρώσεως προσεδέξαντο. λαμβάνει δὲ τῶν αὐτῶν τριῶν δογμάτων γνῶσιν Δαυείδ καὶ λέγει: Μακάριος ἀνήρ, ὃς οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ἐν βουλῇ ἀσεβῶν, καθὼς καὶ οἱ ἰχθύες πορεύονται ἐν σκότει εἰς τὰ βάθη: καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἔστη, καθὼς οἱ δοκοῦντες φοβεῖσθαι τὸν κύριον ἁμαρτάνουσιν ὡς ὁ χοῖρος, καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν, καθὼς τὰ πετεινὰ καθήμενα εἰς ἁρπαγήν. ἔχετε τελείως καὶ περὶ τῆς βρώσεως. πάλιν λέγει Μωϋσῆς: Φάγεσθε πᾶν διχηλοῦν καὶ μαρυκώμενον. τί λέγει; ὅτι τὴν τροφὴν λαμβάνων οἶδεν τὸν τρέφοντα αὐτὸν καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἀναπαυόμενος εὐφραίνεσθαι δοκεῖ. καλῶς εἶπεν βλέπων τὴν ἐντολήν. τί οὖν λέγει; κολλᾶσθε μετὰ τῶν φοβουμένων τὸν κύριον, μετὰ τῶν μελετώντων ὃ ἔλαβον διάσταλμα ῥήματος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ, μετὰ τῶν λαλούντων τὰ διδαιώματα κυρίου καὶ τηρούντων, μετὰ τῶν εἰδότων, ὅτι ἡ μελέτη ἐστὶν ἔργον εὐφροσύνης, καὶ ἀναμαρυκωμένων τὸν λόγον κυρίου. τί δὲ τὸ διχηλοῦν; ὅτι ὁ δίκαιος καὶ ἐν τούτῳ τῷ κόσμῳ περιπατεῖ καὶ τὸν ἅγιον αἰῶνα ἐκδέχεται. βλέπετε, πῶς ἐνομοθέτησεν Μωϋσῆς καλῶς. ἀλλὰ πόθεν ἐκείνοις ταῦτα νοῆσαι ἢ συνιέναι; ἡμεῖς δὲ δικαίως νοήσαντες τὰς ἐντολὰς λαλοῦμεν, ὡς ἠθέλησεν ὁ κύριος. διὰ τοῦτο περιέτεμεν τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν καὶ τὰς καρδίας, ἵνα συνιῶμεν ταῦτα.
pass_a_gloss: For Moses said: You will not eat pig nor eagle nor sharp-sighted one nor crow nor all fish which does not have a scale in itself, he took three doctrines in wisdom. For he says to them in Deuteronomy: And I will make a covenant with this people my righteous deeds. Therefore it is not a command of God not to eat, but Moses spoke in spirit. Therefore he said concerning the pig: You will not be joined, he says, to such people who are like pigs: that is when they squander they forget the Lord, when they are in need they recognize the Lord, just as the pig when it eats does not know the Lord, when it is hungry it cries out, and having eaten again it is silent. You will not eat the eagle nor the sharp-sighted one nor the fish nor the crow: Not, he says, will you be joined or likened to such people who do not know how to provide food for themselves through labor and sweat, but seize what belongs to others in their lawlessness and watch as if walking in innocence and looking around to see whom they might plunder because of their greed, just as these birds alone do not provide food for themselves but sitting idly seek how they might eat the flesh of others, being corrupt in their wickedness. And you will not eat, he says, the smyrnian nor the many-footed one nor the cuttlefish: Not, he says, will you be likened by joining with such people who are unrighteous and already judged to death, just as these little fish are cursed in the deep swimming alone not like the others but dwelling on the ground below the deep. But also you will not eat the hairy-footed one. Why? Not, he says, will you become a corrupter of children nor be likened to such people because the hare exceeds its provision every year: for as many years it lives, it has that many openings. But also you will not eat the hyena: Not, he says, will you become an adulterer nor a corrupter nor be likened to such people. Why? Because this animal changes its nature every year and sometimes is male, sometimes female. But also he rightly hated the weasel. Not, he says, will you become such a one, who we hear are doing lawlessness with the mouth through uncleanness, nor will you join with the unclean ones doing lawlessness with the mouth. For this animal conceives in the mouth. Concerning foods Moses took three doctrines and spoke in spirit in this way: But they received it according to the desire of the flesh as concerning eating. And David receives knowledge of the same three doctrines and says: Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the unrighteous, just as the fish walk in darkness into the depths: And he did not stand in the way of sinners, just as those who seem to fear the Lord sin like the pig, and he did not sit on the seat of the corrupt, just as the birds sitting for plunder. You have it completely concerning eating. Again Moses says: Eat every split-footed and ruminating one. What does he say? That the one receiving food knows the one feeding it and resting on it seems to rejoice. He spoke well seeing the command. What then does he say? Be joined with those fearing the Lord, with those meditating on what they received as a distinction of word in the heart, with those speaking the teachings of the Lord and keeping them, with those knowing that meditation is a work of joy, and ruminating on the word of the Lord. And what is the split-footed one? That the righteous one both walks in this world and awaits the holy age. See how Moses legislated well. But from where will they understand these things or comprehend? We, having understood the commands rightly, speak as the Lord willed. Therefore we have circumcised our ears and hearts so that we might comprehend these things.

pass_b_english: Moses declared, 'You will not eat pig, eagle, osprey, crow, or any fish that lacks scales,' and in doing so he established three principles through spiritual insight. He tells them in Deuteronomy, 'And I will make a covenant with this people, my righteous deeds.' Consequently, the prohibition against eating these creatures is not a command of God in the literal sense; rather, Moses spoke by the Spirit. Regarding the pig, then, he said: 'You must not associate with people like pigs.' These are people who forget the Lord when they are self-indulgent but acknowledge him when they are in need, just as a pig ignores its owner while eating yet squeals when hungry and falls silent again once fed. 'You must not eat the eagle, the osprey, the kite, or the crow,' he said, 'lest you associate with or become like those who refuse to earn their food by labor and sweat, but instead seize what belongs to others through lawlessness. They watch with feigned innocence, scanning for victims to plunder out of greed, just as these birds do not hunt for themselves but sit idly waiting to devour the flesh of others, corrupted by their own wickedness.' 'And you must not eat the ray, the octopus, or the cuttlefish,' he said, 'lest you become like those who are utterly ungodly and already condemned to death. These creatures are cursed in the depths; they do not swim like other fish but dwell on the bottom of the sea.' You must also avoid the hyrax. Why? 'So that you do not become a corrupter of children or resemble such people,' he said, 'for the hyrax gains an additional opening each year it lives, having as many openings as years of life.' You must not eat the hyena either: 'So that you do not become an adulterer or a corrupter or resemble them,' he said. Why? Because this animal changes its nature annually, becoming male one year and female the next. He also rightly rejected the weasel: 'You must not become like those we hear committing lawlessness with their mouths through impurity, nor associate with such unclean women who practice lawlessness with their mouths,' he said, 'for this creature conceives through the mouth.' Thus, concerning food, Moses received three doctrines and spoke them in the Spirit, but the people accepted them according to fleshly desire, treating them as mere dietary rules. David, however, grasped the same three doctrines and said: 'Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked,' just as fish swim in darkness toward the depths; 'nor stand in the way of sinners,' like those who appear to fear the Lord yet sin like the pig; 'nor sit in the seat of scoffers,' like birds perched ready to plunder. You now have the complete spiritual meaning of the food laws. Moses also says, 'Eat every animal that has a split hoof and chews the cud.' What does this mean? The one who receives food knows the one who provides it, and resting on that provision, rejoices. He spoke well because he understood the command spiritually. So what is he saying? 'Associate with those who fear the Lord, with those who meditate on the word they have received as a distinguishing mark in their hearts, with those who speak the Lord's teachings and keep them, with those who know that meditation is a work of joy, and who chew over the word of the Lord.' And what does 'split hoof' signify? That the righteous person walks in this world while awaiting the holy age to come. See how wisely Moses legislated. But how could they have understood or comprehended these things? We, however, having rightly understood the commandments, speak them as the Lord willed. That is why we have circumcised our ears and hearts, so that we might comprehend these things.

review.notes: Pass B introduces gendered terms not present in the Greek source. Specifically, for the clause 'ἀκαθάρτοις ταῖς τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιούσαις ἐν τῷ στόματι' (the unclean ones doing lawlessness with the mouth), Pass B translates it as 'unclean women who practice lawlessness with their mouths', adding 'women' which is not in the Greek text. Additionally, Pass B translates 'καθέδραν λοιμῶν' (seat of the corrupt/ruined) as 'seat of scoffers', which is a significant semantic shift from the Greek 'loimōn' (corrupt/pestilential/ruined).
reasons: Pass B adds 'women' to 'ἀκαθάρτοις ταῖς τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιούσαις ἐν τῷ στόματι' ('unclean ones doing lawlessness with the mouth').
Pass B translates 'καθέδραν λοιμῶν' ('seat of the corrupt') as 'seat of scoffers', which contradicts the Greek 'loimōn'.
